A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALIGN study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, word-association evaluations, psychological-attribute analyses and World Values Survey results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports revised Chinese PPO scores and additional cue-level psychological analyses.

M1.justification: SFT association generation and PPO ranking with Spearman rewards remain unchanged, including the appendix objectives, prompts and reward code. Newly suggested deployment safeguards are explicitly outside the study.

E1.justification: Both versions use US-filtered English SWOW, Mandarin SWOW and US/China WVS questions. The new illustrative cues belong to existing coverage; newly cited cultural benchmarks are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains the vanilla Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-7B models, their SFT/PPO variants, and the Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B WVS baselines. No comparison method is added or replaced within retained experiments.

E3.justification: The reported psychological evaluation loses the Simple-prompt setting from v1 Appendix G. The retained experiments preserve the cue-based 80/10/10 split, training hyperparameters, 221 WVS questions, constrained answer-token procedure and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The supplementary psychological evidence changes substantially: v1's Simple-prompt tables and distribution plots (Tables 12–13; Figures 7–9) disappear, while v2 Appendix F.3/Table 9 adds Halloween and emotions case studies. The preliminary PPO task-format investigations and WVS topic and cultural-shift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: WVS significance reporting changes slightly: v2 Table 4 explicitly states p < 0.05 but omits v1 Table 7's identification of the Wilcoxon test. Psychological Wilcoxon testing remains unchanged, and neither version supplies repeated-run or seed-variability reporting.

E6.justification: Under the same reported settings, Chinese WVS PPO scores change from 0.445/0.143 to 0.334/0.112 for Llama and from 0.412/0.139 to 0.374/0.123 for Qwen (JSD/EMD; v1 Table 7 versus v2 Table 4). This reverses Llama's SFT-versus-PPO ranking on Chinese WVS. Simple-prompt results are removed and cue-level results are added, while the main lexical scores and other WVS table entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The SFT/PPO objectives and hybrid tension-set selection formula are retained in substance. The new standard JSD/EMD formulas explain existing metrics rather than introduce a new theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The central lexical-to-value transfer and small-model-versus-large-model claims remain. v2 qualifies initial cultural leanings as relative model comparisons, emphasizes culture-specific alignment, and omits concreteness from its introductory and concluding summary claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability boundaries: models are not clean national-culture proxies, effects on non-target cultures are untested, and transfer to low-resource settings remains unresolved. Section 7 adds stereotyping risks, contextual adapter/fallback recommendations and uncertainty about why SFT and PPO work differently across cultures.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link to its release statement, WVS respondent counts and more explicit metric documentation. Hardware, libraries, training hyperparameters, prompts and reward implementation remain substantively unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted discussion of FORK, BLEnD and CulturalBench, and cites CultureLLM to motivate culture-specific models. Several earlier references, including CAVA, CARE and QualBench, disappear, while the central distinction from Dai et al.'s concurrent association work remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the main narrative are rewritten, framework subsections are reorganized, and association evaluation is restructured into intrinsic and extrinsic sections. Appendix B's PPO-format discussion becomes Appendix A.3, with corresponding reorganization of later appendices.

P2.justification: v1 Tables 1–6 are consolidated into v2 Tables 1–3, Figure 1 moves to the first page, and multiple displays are resized or relocated. Simple-prompt tables and plots are removed, a substantial cue-example table is added, and scatter-plot axis labels are revised while plotted points are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 improves explanations, scope qualifications and access information, but removes meaningful prompt-sensitivity evidence. For example, v1 reports English Qwen-SFT concreteness of 3.535 with the Complex prompt and 3.762 with the Simple prompt, against a human median of 3.644 (Tables 5 and 12). The new two-cue examples aid interpretation without restoring that robustness check. These gains and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
